note: Draft layer written by Claude on 2026-10-25 where Wikidata and Pantheon are thin; each row names the Wikipedia article it was written from. Waiting for the judge.

rows.name: Founding of the Round City (Madinat al-Salam)
rows.desc: Caliph al-Mansur laid out his circular walled capital on the west bank of the Tigris near the old village of Baghdad.

rows.name: Al-Mansur
rows.desc: The second Abbasid caliph founded Baghdad and ruled from the Round City until his death on pilgrimage.

rows.name: Palace of the Golden Gate
rows.desc: The caliphal palace with its green dome stood at the centre of the Round City beside the main mosque.

rows.name: Mosque of al-Mansur in the Round City
rows.desc: The first congregational mosque of Baghdad was built next to the caliph's palace in the centre of the Round City.

rows.name: Markets moved out to al-Karkh
rows.desc: Al-Mansur removed the markets from the Round City to the southern suburb of al-Karkh, which grew into the commercial heart of the west bank.

rows.name: Khuld Palace on the Tigris
rows.desc: Al-Mansur built the al-Khuld palace on the Tigris bank outside the Round City, later favoured by Harun al-Rashid.

rows.name: Al-Rusafa built for the heir al-Mahdi
rows.desc: An army camp and palace complex for the heir al-Mahdi was laid out on the east bank, beginning East Baghdad.

rows.name: Al-Mansur tries to demolish the Taq Kasra
rows.desc: According to the chronicles al-Mansur began pulling down the Sasanian palace at Ctesiphon for building material but gave up because of the cost.

rows.name: Death of Abu Hanifa
rows.desc: The founder of the Hanafi school of law died in prison in Baghdad and was buried in the quarter later called al-Adhamiyya.

rows.name: Death of Ibn Ishaq
rows.desc: The author of the earliest surviving biography of the Prophet, written for the Abbasid court, died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Al-Mahdi
rows.desc: The third Abbasid caliph ruled from Baghdad and favoured the east bank quarter of al-Rusafa.

rows.name: Al-Hadi
rows.desc: Al-Mahdi's son reigned for just over a year before his sudden death in 786.

rows.name: Birth of al-Ma'mun
rows.desc: Harun al-Rashid's son al-Ma'mun was born in Baghdad to a Persian concubine on the night of his father's accession.

rows.name: Birth of al-Amin
rows.desc: Al-Amin, son of Harun and Zubaydah, was born in Baghdad and became heir ahead of his elder half-brother.

rows.name: Harun al-Rashid
rows.desc: The fifth Abbasid caliph ruled at the height of Abbasid wealth, spending his later years mostly at Raqqa.

rows.name: Yahya ibn Khalid the Barmakid
rows.desc: Harun's former tutor ran the administration as vizier with his sons until the family's fall.

rows.name: Ja'far ibn Yahya
rows.desc: The Barmakid companion and vizier of Harun al-Rashid, famous in later literature, lived in a great palace on the east bank.

rows.name: Al-Fadl ibn Yahya
rows.desc: Ja'far's elder brother was tutor to al-Amin and a leading Barmakid official before his imprisonment.

rows.name: Zubaydah bint Ja'far
rows.desc: Harun's wife and cousin was a great builder and patron who died in Baghdad in 831.

rows.name: Abu Yusuf, chief qadi
rows.desc: The Hanafi jurist served as the first chief judge of the empire in Baghdad under Harun.

rows.name: Kitab al-Kharaj of Abu Yusuf
rows.desc: Abu Yusuf wrote his treatise on land tax and public finance for Harun al-Rashid.

rows.name: First paper mill in Baghdad
rows.desc: Under Barmakid patronage paper making was established in Baghdad, and paper soon replaced papyrus and parchment in the chanceries.

rows.name: Death of Musa al-Kazim
rows.desc: The seventh Twelver imam died in Harun's prison in Baghdad and was buried in the Quraysh cemetery, the later al-Kazimiyya.

rows.name: Shrine of al-Kazimiyya
rows.desc: The tombs of Musa al-Kazim and later Muhammad al-Jawad became a major Shi'i shrine north of the Round City.

rows.name: Charlemagne's envoys at the Abbasid court
rows.desc: Frankish envoys sent by Charlemagne reached Harun al-Rashid, beginning an exchange that brought the elephant Abul-Abbas to Aachen.

rows.name: Fall of the Barmakids
rows.desc: Harun had Ja'far executed near al-Anbar and imprisoned Yahya and al-Fadl, ending the family's seventeen years of power.

rows.name: First Baghdad hospital (bimaristan)
rows.desc: A hospital modelled on the Persian school of Gundeshapur was founded in Baghdad in Harun's reign.

rows.name: Jibril ibn Bukhtishu
rows.desc: The Nestorian court physician from the Gundeshapur family served Harun and his sons in Baghdad.

rows.name: Abu Nuwas
rows.desc: The poet of wine and love was the leading court poet of Harun and al-Amin and died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Death of Ibrahim al-Mawsili
rows.desc: The leading singer and composer of Harun's court died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Ishaq al-Mawsili
rows.desc: Ibrahim's son was the foremost musician and music theorist of the early Abbasid court and died in Baghdad in 850.

rows.name: Al-Shafi'i in Baghdad
rows.desc: The founder of the Shafi'i school taught in Baghdad before moving to Egypt.

rows.name: Birth of Ahmad ibn Hanbal
rows.desc: The future founder of the Hanbali school was born in Baghdad.

rows.name: Patriarch Timothy I of the Church of the East
rows.desc: The Nestorian patriarch, resident in Baghdad, debated Islam with al-Mahdi and sponsored translation of Aristotle.

rows.name: Al-Waqidi
rows.desc: The historian of the Prophet's campaigns served as a qadi in Baghdad and died there.

rows.name: Death of Ma'ruf al-Karkhi
rows.desc: The ascetic of al-Karkh died and his tomb on the west bank became a much visited shrine.

rows.name: Siege of Baghdad (812 to 813)
rows.desc: The armies of al-Ma'mun under Tahir ibn Husayn and Harthama besieged al-Amin in Baghdad, wrecking much of the city.

rows.name: Tahir ibn Husayn
rows.desc: Al-Ma'mun's general led the siege from the west and later founded the Tahirid dynasty of governors.

rows.name: Harthama ibn A'yan
rows.desc: The veteran commander attacked from the east bank during the siege.

rows.name: Killing of al-Amin
rows.desc: Al-Amin was captured while trying to escape by boat and was killed by Tahir's soldiers.

rows.name: Anti-caliphate of Ibrahim ibn al-Mahdi
rows.desc: Baghdad notables proclaimed Ibrahim ibn al-Mahdi caliph in protest at al-Ma'mun's choice of an Alid heir.

rows.name: Revolt of Ibn Tabataba and Abu al-Saraya
rows.desc: An Alid revolt broke out at Kufa during the civil war and briefly spread through lower Iraq.

rows.name: Al-Ma'mun enters Baghdad
rows.desc: Al-Ma'mun arrived from Khurasan, ending the civil war and restoring Baghdad as the capital.

rows.name: Al-Ma'mun
rows.desc: The caliph patronized scholars and translators and imposed the doctrine of the created Quran.

rows.name: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Mus'abi
rows.desc: The Tahirid governor and police chief of Baghdad ran the city for nearly thirty years and enforced the mihna.

rows.name: House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma)
rows.desc: The caliphal library and translation centre flourished under al-Ma'mun and became a symbol of Abbasid learning.

rows.name: Al-Khwarizmi
rows.desc: The mathematician and astronomer worked at the House of Wisdom; his name gave the word algorithm.

rows.name: Al-Jabr of al-Khwarizmi
rows.desc: Al-Khwarizmi's book on calculation by completion and balancing founded algebra as a discipline.

rows.name: Zij al-Sindhind of al-Khwarizmi
rows.desc: Al-Khwarizmi compiled astronomical tables based on Indian methods.

rows.name: Al-Shammasiyya observatory
rows.desc: Al-Ma'mun's astronomers made systematic observations at al-Shammasiyya in northeastern Baghdad.
rows.wikipedia: Astronomy in the medieval Islamic world

rows.name: Habash al-Hasib
rows.desc: The astronomer of al-Ma'mun's circle produced tables and early trigonometric functions.

rows.name: Al-Hajjaj ibn Matar translates the Almagest
rows.desc: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf ibn Matar produced Arabic versions of Euclid's Elements and Ptolemy's Almagest.

rows.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
rows.desc: The Nestorian physician led a team that translated Galen and much Greek science into Syriac and Arabic.

rows.name: Al-Kindi
rows.desc: The first major philosopher writing in Arabic worked under al-Ma'mun and al-Mu'tasim and supervised translations.

rows.name: Banu Musa brothers
rows.desc: Three brothers, sons of Musa ibn Shakir, sponsored translators and wrote on mathematics and mechanics.

rows.name: Book of Ingenious Devices
rows.desc: The Banu Musa described about a hundred automata and trick vessels.

rows.name: Al-Jahiz in Baghdad and Samarra
rows.desc: The Basran prose master spent much of his career at court in Baghdad and Samarra.

rows.name: Ibn Sa'd
rows.desc: Al-Waqidi's secretary compiled the great biographical dictionary of early Muslims in Baghdad.

rows.name: Arib al-Ma'muniyya
rows.desc: The celebrated singer and poet performed for several caliphs in Baghdad and Samarra.

rows.name: The mihna begins
rows.desc: Al-Ma'mun ordered judges and scholars to affirm that the Quran was created, and the Baghdad governor examined them.

rows.name: Trial and flogging of Ahmad ibn Hanbal
rows.desc: Ibn Hanbal refused to affirm the created Quran and was flogged before al-Mu'tasim, becoming a popular hero.

rows.name: Al-Mutawakkil ends the mihna
rows.desc: Al-Mutawakkil abandoned the doctrine of the created Quran and the inquisition.

rows.name: Death of Ahmad ibn Hanbal
rows.desc: Huge crowds attended the funeral of Ibn Hanbal in Baghdad.

rows.name: Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal
rows.desc: Ibn Hanbal's vast collection of hadith, arranged by transmitter, was completed by his son.

rows.name: Death of Muhammad al-Jawad
rows.desc: The ninth Twelver imam died in Baghdad and was buried beside his grandfather at al-Kazimiyya.

rows.name: Death of al-Harith al-Muhasibi
rows.desc: The early Sufi psychologist of the self died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Al-Mu'tasim moves the capital to Samarra
rows.desc: Friction between his Turkish guard and the Baghdadis led al-Mu'tasim to found a new capital up the Tigris.

rows.name: Founding of Samarra (Surra Man Ra'a)
rows.desc: A vast new palace city spread for kilometres along the east bank of the Tigris.

rows.name: Dar al-Khilafa (Jawsaq al-Khaqani) at Samarra
rows.desc: The main caliphal palace at Samarra overlooked the Tigris with gardens, courts and a polo ground.

rows.name: Death of al-Mu'tasim
rows.desc: The founder of Samarra died there in January 842.

rows.name: Death of al-Wathiq
rows.desc: Al-Wathiq, the last caliph to uphold the mihna, died at Samarra.

rows.name: Great Mosque of Samarra and the Malwiya
rows.desc: Al-Mutawakkil built what was then the largest mosque in the world with its spiral minaret.

rows.name: Al-Mutawakkil orders the tomb of Husayn razed
rows.desc: Al-Mutawakkil had the shrine of Husayn at Karbala destroyed and the land flooded and ploughed.

rows.name: Al-Ja'fariyya (al-Mutawakkiliyya) and the Abu Dulaf Mosque
rows.desc: Al-Mutawakkil built a new city north of Samarra with a congregational mosque that survives as the Abu Dulaf Mosque.

rows.name: Assassination of al-Mutawakkil
rows.desc: Turkish officers in league with his son al-Muntasir murdered the caliph at al-Ja'fariyya.

rows.name: Anarchy at Samarra
rows.desc: Turkish commanders made and unmade four caliphs in nine years.

rows.name: Civil war and siege of Baghdad (865 to 866)
rows.desc: Al-Musta'in fled to Baghdad and was besieged there by the forces of al-Mu'tazz from Samarra.

rows.name: Death of Ali al-Hadi
rows.desc: The tenth Twelver imam, held under watch at Samarra, died and was buried in his house there.

rows.name: Death of Hasan al-Askari
rows.desc: The eleventh imam died at Samarra and was buried beside his father.

rows.name: Beginning of the Minor Occultation
rows.desc: Twelver Shi'is hold that the twelfth imam went into hiding at Samarra and spoke through four deputies in Baghdad.

rows.name: Al-Askari Shrine
rows.desc: The tombs of the tenth and eleventh imams at Samarra grew into a major shrine.

rows.name: Al-Buhturi
rows.desc: The court poet celebrated the palaces and caliphs of Samarra.

rows.name: Ibn Khordadbeh's Book of Roads and Kingdoms
rows.desc: The postmaster general described the routes and revenues of the caliphate from the capital.

rows.name: Al-Baladhuri
rows.desc: The historian of the Arab conquests was a courtier in Baghdad and Samarra and wrote Futuh al-Buldan.

rows.name: Ibn Qutayba
rows.desc: The scholar and essayist taught in Baghdad in his last years and died there.

rows.name: Al-Mubarrad
rows.desc: The Basran grammarian taught in Baghdad and died there.

rows.name: Caliphs return to Baghdad
rows.desc: Al-Mu'tadid made Baghdad the permanent capital again and Samarra declined.

rows.name: Al-Ya'qubi's Book of Countries
rows.desc: Al-Ya'qubi described Baghdad's quarters, canals and markets and the rise and fall of Samarra.

rows.name: East bank caliphal palace (Dar al-Khilafa)
rows.desc: From al-Mu'tadid onward the caliphs lived in the Hasani palace complex on the east bank, enlarged with the Taj and Thurayya palaces.

rows.name: Thabit ibn Qurra
rows.desc: The Sabian mathematician from Harran translated and wrote on geometry and astronomy in Baghdad, dying there in 901.

rows.name: Death of Ibn al-Rumi
rows.desc: The satirical poet died in Baghdad, reportedly poisoned.

rows.name: Death of al-Junayd
rows.desc: The master of the sober Baghdad school of Sufism died in the city.

rows.name: Al-Muqtadir
rows.desc: His long reign saw palace intrigue, fiscal crisis and lavish court display.

rows.name: Ali ibn Isa ibn al-Jarrah
rows.desc: The reforming vizier tried to balance the budget and founded hospitals.

rows.name: Banu al-Furat viziers
rows.desc: The rival bureaucratic clan of Ibn al-Furat held the vizierate three times under al-Muqtadir.

rows.name: Byzantine embassy received by al-Muqtadir
rows.desc: Byzantine envoys were led through palaces with the famous silver tree to impress them with caliphal wealth.

rows.name: Abu Bakr al-Razi directs a Baghdad hospital
rows.desc: The great physician is reported to have headed a hospital in Baghdad and chosen its site.

rows.name: Hospitals of Sinan ibn Thabit
rows.desc: Sinan ibn Thabit supervised new hospitals in Baghdad and introduced licensing of physicians.

rows.name: Ibn Fadlan sets out for the Volga Bulgars
rows.desc: An embassy left Baghdad for the Volga; Ibn Fadlan's account describes the Rus.

rows.name: Execution of al-Hallaj
rows.desc: The mystic who said I am the Truth was publicly executed in Baghdad after a long trial.

rows.name: Al-Tabari
rows.desc: The historian and Quran commentator lived and taught in Baghdad until his death in 923.

rows.name: History of the Prophets and Kings
rows.desc: Al-Tabari completed his universal history, the main source for early Islamic history.
rows.wikipedia: History of the Prophets and Kings

rows.name: Qarmatians threaten Kufa and Baghdad
rows.desc: Qarmatian forces from Bahrayn raided Kufa and advanced toward Baghdad.

rows.name: Saadia Gaon
rows.desc: The gaon of the Sura academy, then based in Baghdad, translated the Bible into Arabic and died in the city.

rows.name: Death of al-Muqtadir
rows.desc: The caliph was killed in battle against the troops of Mu'nis outside Baghdad.

rows.name: Hanbali street campaigns of al-Barbahari
rows.desc: Followers of al-Barbahari raided taverns and attacked opponents until the caliph banned them.

rows.name: Ibn Ra'iq becomes amir al-umara
rows.desc: Military power passed from the caliph to a commander-in-chief, the amir al-umara.

rows.name: Death of Ibn Muqla
rows.desc: The vizier who systematized proportional Arabic script died in prison after his hand was cut off.

rows.name: Abu Bishr Matta ibn Yunus
rows.desc: The Nestorian logician led the Baghdad Aristotelians until his death.

rows.name: Al-Farabi in Baghdad
rows.desc: The Second Teacher studied logic in Baghdad before leaving for Syria.

rows.name: Hamdanid Nasir al-Dawla in Baghdad
rows.desc: The Hamdanid amir of Mosul briefly held Baghdad as amir al-umara.

rows.name: Tuzun blinds al-Muttaqi
rows.desc: The Turkish commander Tuzun deposed and blinded the caliph al-Muttaqi at al-Sindiyya west of Baghdad.

rows.name: Buyid conquest of Baghdad
rows.desc: Ahmad ibn Buya entered Baghdad and took the title Mu'izz al-Dawla, leaving the caliph a figurehead.

rows.name: Mu'izz al-Dawla
rows.desc: The Buyid amir ruled Iraq from Baghdad for over twenty years.

rows.name: Al-Mustakfi blinded and deposed
rows.desc: Mu'izz al-Dawla had the caliph seized and blinded and installed al-Muti.

rows.name: Ashura mourning publicly observed
rows.desc: Mu'izz al-Dawla ordered public mourning for Husayn on Ashura, a lasting Shi'i ritual in Baghdad.

rows.name: Kitab al-Aghani
rows.desc: Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani compiled his great anthology of songs and poets in Baghdad.

rows.name: Yahya ibn Adi
rows.desc: The Jacobite Christian logician headed the Baghdad school of philosophy.

rows.name: Burning of al-Karkh
rows.desc: During factional fighting a large part of al-Karkh was destroyed by fire.

rows.name: Adud al-Dawla
rows.desc: The most powerful Buyid ruled from Baghdad, repaired canals and rebuilt quarters.

rows.name: Adud al-Dawla rebuilds the shrines of Karbala
rows.desc: The Buyid ruler rebuilt the shrine of Husayn at Karbala.

rows.name: Al-Adudi Hospital
rows.desc: Adud al-Dawla founded a large teaching hospital on the west bank on the site of the old Khuld palace.

rows.name: Al-Fihrist of Ibn al-Nadim
rows.desc: The Baghdad bookseller catalogued all books known in Arabic.

rows.name: Observatory of Sharaf al-Dawla
rows.desc: The Buyid amir built an observatory in his palace garden where al-Kuhi and Abu al-Wafa observed.

rows.name: Dar al-Ilm of Sabur ibn Ardashir
rows.desc: The Buyid vizier founded a public library in al-Karkh with over ten thousand volumes.

rows.name: Death of Ibn al-Bawwab
rows.desc: The calligrapher who refined Ibn Muqla's script died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Nahj al-Balagha
rows.desc: Al-Sharif al-Radi compiled the sermons and letters attributed to Ali.

rows.name: Death of al-Shaykh al-Mufid
rows.desc: The leading Twelver theologian of Buyid Baghdad died and was buried at al-Kazimiyya.

rows.name: Qadiri creed
rows.desc: Caliph al-Qadir issued a Sunni creed condemning Mu'tazilis and Shi'is.

rows.name: Ayyarun in Baghdad
rows.desc: Urban gangs of ayyarun dominated quarters of Baghdad in the late Buyid period.

rows.name: Al-Mawardi
rows.desc: The Shafi'i jurist wrote on the theory of the caliphate and died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya
rows.desc: Al-Mawardi set out the constitutional ordinances of the caliphate.

rows.name: Tughril enters Baghdad
rows.desc: The Seljuk sultan Tughril entered Baghdad and ended Buyid rule.

rows.name: Al-Basasiri proclaims the Fatimid caliph
rows.desc: The Turkish commander al-Basasiri seized Baghdad for the Fatimids for about a year.

rows.name: Tarikh Baghdad
rows.desc: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi compiled a vast biographical history of the city's scholars.

rows.name: Nizamiyya of Baghdad
rows.desc: Nizam al-Mulk founded a great Shafi'i college on the east bank, opened in 1067.

rows.name: Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi
rows.desc: The first professor of the Nizamiyya taught Shafi'i law there.

rows.name: Al-Ghazali at the Nizamiyya
rows.desc: Al-Ghazali taught at the Nizamiyya before leaving in a spiritual crisis.

rows.name: The Incoherence of the Philosophers
rows.desc: Al-Ghazali attacked the Aristotelian philosophers.

rows.name: Death of Malik-Shah
rows.desc: Malik-Shah I died suddenly in Baghdad.

rows.name: Walls of East Baghdad
rows.desc: Caliph al-Mustazhir began a new wall around East Baghdad.

rows.name: Abd al-Qadir al-Gilani
rows.desc: The Hanbali preacher whose school became the Qadiriyya order lived in Baghdad from 1095.

rows.name: Founding of Hilla
rows.desc: The Mazyadid amir Sadaqa ibn Mansur founded Hilla on the Euphrates near Babylon.

rows.name: Death of Ibn Aqil
rows.desc: The Hanbali theologian died in Baghdad.

rows.name: Bab al-Wastani
rows.desc: The surviving gate of the Abbasid walls of East Baghdad.

rows.name: Siege of Baghdad (1157)
rows.desc: Caliph al-Muqtafi resisted a Seljuk siege, restoring caliphal independence in Iraq.

rows.name: Death of Abd al-Qadir al-Gilani
rows.desc: His tomb at Bab al-Shaykh became the centre of the Qadiri order.

rows.name: Benjamin of Tudela visits Baghdad
rows.desc: The Jewish traveller described the caliph and Baghdad's Jewish community.

rows.name: Al-Nasir li-Din Allah
rows.desc: The caliph restored Abbasid power in Iraq and reorganized futuwwa brotherhoods.

rows.name: Ibn Jubayr visits Baghdad
rows.desc: The Andalusian traveller described Baghdad's colleges, preachers and hospital.

rows.name: Ibn al-Jawzi
rows.desc: The Hanbali preacher and historian of Baghdad wrote al-Muntazam.

rows.name: Abbasid Palace
rows.desc: A brick courtyard building of the late Abbasid period survives near the Tigris.

rows.name: Zumurrud Khatun Mausoleum
rows.desc: A tomb with a muqarnas dome was built near the shrine of Ma'ruf al-Karkhi.

rows.name: Al-Mustansir
rows.desc: The caliph founded the Mustansiriyya college.

rows.name: Mustansiriyya Madrasa
rows.desc: Al-Mustansir built a college teaching all four Sunni schools, with a hospital, baths and water clock.

rows.name: Al-Wasiti's illustrated Maqamat
rows.desc: Yahya al-Wasiti copied and painted a famous manuscript of al-Hariri's Maqamat.

rows.name: Yaqut al-Musta'simi
rows.desc: The secretary of the last caliph became the most famous Arabic calligrapher.

rows.name: Safi al-Din al-Urmawi
rows.desc: The music theorist and court musician survived the Mongol sack.

rows.name: Al-Musta'sim
rows.desc: The last Abbasid caliph of Baghdad.

rows.name: Ibn al-Alqami
rows.desc: The Shi'i vizier of al-Musta'sim, later accused of helping the Mongols.

rows.name: Abbasid army routed near Baghdad
rows.desc: The Mongols flooded the Abbasid army's camp west of Baghdad by breaking dykes.

rows.name: Mongol siege of Baghdad
rows.desc: Hulagu's army besieged and stormed Baghdad, which surrendered on 10 February.

rows.name: Hulagu Khan at Baghdad
rows.desc: The Mongol commander led the siege.

rows.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi with Hulagu
rows.desc: The astronomer accompanied Hulagu during the siege.

rows.name: Sack of Baghdad
rows.desc: Mongol troops sacked Baghdad for about a week, killing many and destroying libraries.

rows.name: Execution of al-Musta'sim
rows.desc: The last caliph was executed by the Mongols.

rows.name: Loss of the House of Wisdom
rows.desc: The libraries of Baghdad were destroyed in the sack.
